Text: The {{c1::Single Responsibility Principle}} states that a class should have only one reason to change, promoting high {{c2::cohesion}}.
Extra: A cohesive class keeps related variables and logic together. By focusing on a single task, it communicates via well-defined boundaries.

Text: The {{c1::Open/Closed Principle}} states that software entities should be open for {{c2::extension}} but closed for {{c3::modification}}.
Extra: Extensibility is achieved via polymorphism, interfaces, and abstract classes. This keeps the original, verified bytecode untouched.

Text: The {{c1::Liskov Substitution Principle}} requires that subtypes must be substitutable for their {{c2::parent types}} without altering program correctness.
Extra: Subclasses must not strengthen preconditions (like throwing new checked exceptions) or weaken postconditions (like returning null).

Text: Under LSP, a subclass must not {{c1::strengthen}} preconditions or {{c2::weaken}} postconditions.
Extra: Violations cause runtime crashes when a client attempts to use a subclass through a parent reference.

Text: The {{c1::Interface Segregation Principle}} states that clients should not be forced to depend on methods they do not {{c2::use}}.
Extra: This prevents "fat" interfaces from coupling unrelated components and causing compile-time ripple effects.

Text: The {{c1::Dependency Inversion Principle}} requires that high-level modules depend on {{c2::abstractions}} rather than concrete implementations.
Extra: Abstractions decouple the compile-time relationship, enabling easy mock substitution for unit testing.

Text: {{c1::Dependency Injection}} is the technique of passing concrete implementations into a class, typically via the {{c2::constructor}}.
Extra: Passing dependencies from the outside decouples class instantiation from class behavior and facilitates mocking.

Text: {{c1::DRY}} stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, which asserts that every piece of system logic must have a {{c2::single, authoritative}} representation.
Extra: Preventing duplicate code blocks ensures that bug fixes and changes only need to be applied in one place.

Text: {{c1::YAGNI}} is a principle suggesting that you should not add functionality until it is {{c2::necessary}}.
Extra: Speculative coding wastes developer time and locks the design into incorrect assumptions.

Text: {{c1::Coupling}} measures class interdependence, whereas {{c2::cohesion}} measures class focus on a single responsibility.
Extra: The goal is loose coupling and high cohesion to keep systems maintainable.

Text: Reusing behavior by enclosing instance variables rather than extending classes is known as {{c1::composition over inheritance}}.
Extra: Composition is a "has-a" relationship, which prevents the subclass from being coupled to base class internals.

Text: Validating parameters at method boundaries using `Objects.requireNonNull()` is an example of {{c1::defensive programming}} and is a {{c2::fail-fast}} approach.
Extra: Catching invalid inputs early prevents corrupted states or cryptic exceptions deep within the execution stack.
